\chapter{Kikuchi LDC — Decomposition}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.KikuchiLDC.LDC.Decomposition
\section{Overview}

This module covers \S6 of the Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar argument: the
hypergraph decomposition step. Given $3$-uniform hypergraphs $H_1, \dots, H_k$ on
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and a threshold $d$, one isolates the heavy pairs, i.e.\ the vertex
pairs of degree more than $d$, bounds their number by $3m/d$, and splits each $H_i$ into
a residual part whose pair-degrees are at most $d$ and a part carried by the heavy pairs.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Heavy pairs of a hypergraph]
\lean{heavyPairs}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b003}
\uses{Hypergraph, Hypergraph.degree}
For a hypergraph $H$ on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and a threshold $d$, the set of heavy pairs
\[
  P \;=\; \{\, Q \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n \;:\; \abs{Q} = 2, \ \deg_H(Q) > d \,\},
\]
realised as the collection of two-element sets $\{u,v\}$ whose degree in $H$ exceeds $d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Counting heavy pairs]
\lean{heavy_pair_count_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b006}
\uses{Hypergraph, Hypergraph.IsUniform, Hypergraph.degree, heavyPairs}
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and let $d > 0$. Then the number
of heavy pairs satisfies
\[
  \abs{P} \cdot d \;\le\; 3 \, \abs{H},
\]
where $P$ is the set of pairs of degree more than $d$; equivalently $\abs{P} \le 3m/d$
for $m = \abs{H}$ edges, since each $3$-edge contributes exactly three pairs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hypergraph decomposition]
\lean{hypergraph_decomposition}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b003,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b008
}
\uses{Hypergraph, Hypergraph.IsMatching, Hypergraph.IsUniform, Hypergraph.degree, Hypergraph.pairDegreeBound, NormalLDC}
Let $L$ be a normal form locally decodable code with message length $k$ and block length
$n$, given by the $3$-uniform matchings $H_i$, and let $d > 0$. Then there is a family of
hypergraphs $H'_i$ on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, indexed by $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, such that each
$H'_i \subseteq H_i$, each $H'_i$ is $3$-uniform and a matching, and the combined
hypergraph $\bigcup_{i} H'_i$ satisfies the pair-degree bound $d$.


\emph{Placeholder.}  The Lean statement omits the paper's counting clause
$|H_i| = |H'_i| + |G_i|$, and without it the empty hypergraph satisfies every remaining
clause --- which is exactly the witness the proof supplies (\texttt{use fun \_ => \ensuremath{\emptyset}}).
Lemma 6.1's content is that few edges are removed; that is \emph{not} formalised here.
\end{theorem}
